title: People at work (professions)
brief: First batch of the style: create parts/flat-vector/style (palette below) and the generator parts/flat-vector/person (params: pose stand|walk|run|wave|point|think|cheer|talk|sit|hold, expression smile|neutral|open|surprised|sad|angry|laugh, skin 6 tones, hair style + colour, top/bottom/shoes types + colours, hat, accessory, held prop, flip, vx; ~1000 px tall at s 1; facing right). Then one preset part per profession that only fixes outfit, hat, accessory and prop. Generic uniforms only: no real police/army/airline insignia or brand logos.

title: Everyday people, ages and roles
brief: Presets of flat-vector/person (generator exists). Cover ages (child, teen, adult, elder via a body/age param if the generator has one, otherwise add an `age` param to the generator first), families, hobbies, moods and archetypes. Respectful, diverse, no stereotypes.
notes: Added `age` (adult|teen|child|toddler|elder) and prop `cane` to flat-vector/person (v1.1.0, existing presets unchanged). Skipped 'student with backpack' (duplicate of flat-vector/student).

title: Mammals
brief: Create the generator parts/flat-vector/quadruped (body proportions, legs, tail, ears, snout, pattern spots|stripes|none, walk/run/sit/idle, flip, vx) and parts/flat-vector/animal-face for heads, then one preset per species. Recognisable silhouettes and colours; cute but not cartoon-brand-like.
notes: New generators flat-vector/quadruped (proportions, ears, tails, horns, manes, patterns; stand/walk/run/idle/sit/lie/graze) and flat-vector/animal-face (front-facing heads, 7 expressions). 97 quadruped presets; standalone parts for sea mammals (8), apes, sloth, bat, kangaroo, wallaby, meerkat. All 114 names built.

title: Birds, sea life, reptiles and bugs
brief: Generators: parts/flat-vector/bird (perch/fly/flap), parts/flat-vector/fish (swim cycle), parts/flat-vector/bug; then presets. Reptiles may get their own small generator.
notes: New generators flat-vector/bird (10 beaks, crests, combs, fan/train tails, stand/walk/hop/peck/perch/fly/glide/swim/idle), flat-vector/fish (shapes, hammer/bill/whisker heads, puffed), flat-vector/bug (side/top view, butterfly/moth/clear/shell wings, glow, jumper legs) and flat-vector/reptile (lizard/croc/snake/coil/turtle bodies). 40 bird, 10 fish, 15 bug, 14 reptile presets; 23 standalone sea creatures, amphibians and crawlers. All 102 names built.

title: Food and drink
brief: Small prop generators where it helps (fruit/round food, plate + dish, cup/glass/bottle, packaged food without brands), then presets. No brand names or logos.
notes: New prop generators flat-vector/fruit (8 shapes, textures, stems/calyx/crown, cut halves with pits, roll/bounce/pop), flat-vector/dish (plate/bowl/deepbowl/tray/board/pan/basket/katori with liquid/grains/strands/chunks/leafy/pieces/balls fills, garnish, steam) and flat-vector/drink (mug/cup/teacup/glasses/wine/stemmed/bottle/can/carton/jar/takeaway; liquid, foam, straw, ice, steam, plain labels). 20 fruit, 16 dish and 15 drink presets; 67 standalone foods. Props are hero size at s = 1 (use s 0.2-0.3 beside a person). All 118 names built; no brands, text or logos.

title: Home, furniture and household objects
brief: Furniture and household objects drawn front/side-on, anchored at the base. Generic designs only.
notes: 128 standalone flat-vector home props (no generator). Two size classes: room-scale furniture/appliances/fixtures match a flat-vector person at s = 1 (1 m ≈ 560 px); small handheld items are hero size at s = 1 (use s 0.2-0.3 beside a person). Wall items centre on (x, y) (default y 760); ceiling lights hang from (x, y) (default y 0). Item-specific anims (tick, ring, flicker, glow, on, swing, spin, roll, blow, steam, bubbles, water, sway, open...). 'bowl' not built: covered by flat-vector/dish (vessel bowl, fill none). No brands, logos or text (calendar shows day numbers only).

title: Technology and devices
brief: Devices and tech props; screens can show simple generic UI (no real app logos).
notes: humanoid robot covered by flat-vector/robot-person; bluetooth symbol skipped (trademarked logo); walkman -> portable-cassette-player and polaroid camera -> instant-camera (trademark-free slugs); 'mouse' slug taken by the animal, use computer-mouse; the 7 rebuilt in run 08 (computer-mouse, earbuds, charging-cable, podcast-mic, satellite-dish, cpu-chip, ring-light)

title: Tools, work and industry
brief: Hand tools, power tools and industrial objects.
notes: ladder and toolbox already existed (06); key covered by flat-vector/keys; iron tool covered by flat-vector/iron. Slugs: saw->hand-saw, level->spirit-level, hose->garden-hose, barrier->road-barrier, gloves->work-gloves, goggles->safety-goggles, file tool->metal-file, crane->construction-crane, generator->power-generator, torch flame->flaming-torch, bucket of water->water-bucket, sand bag->sand-bag, cog wheel->gear-pair (interlocking gears), measuring tape->sewing-tape-measure (tailor's tape). Deleted in review, rebuild next run: hand drill (unreadable crank drill), fishing net (looked like a racket), vise (two slabs, unrecognisable), harvester (did not read as a combine). Run 2026-11-17 (with 09): rebuilt hand-drill, fishing-net, vise. combine-harvester failed review twice more (read as a tractor with a fan / tall box with a pinwheel) – orchestrator should draw it directly next time. Run 2026-11-17 (with 10): combine-harvester drawn directly by the orchestrator (header with reel, feeder, cab, grain tank, unloading pipe).

title: Vehicles and transport
brief: Side-view vehicles with optional wheel spin and vx; generic designs, no logos.
notes: Vehicle convention set by flat-vector/car (reference): side view facing right, wheels on y, params x,y,s,color,color2,anim(none/drive/bob/pop),vx,flip; boats sit on a waterline at y; aircraft anim fly. Skipped: 'tractor vehicle' (flat-vector/tractor exists), 'ev charger' (flat-vector/electric-car-charger), 'kick scooter' (flat-vector/electric-scooter). Slugs: scooter->motor-scooter, jet->private-jet, tank->army-tank, train station sign->station-sign. Deleted in review, rebuild next run: glider (wing and body unreadable after a redraw), go-kart (thin lines, floating steering wheel after a redraw), space shuttle (read as a plain white jet). Redrawn after review: airplane, private-jet, auto-rickshaw, tugboat, harbour-crane (was a tower crane duplicate). Run 2026-11-17 (with 10): rebuilt glider (orchestrator redrew it: diagonal long wings, T-tail), go-kart (orchestrator redrew it), space-shuttle (vertical launch stack with orange tank and boosters).

title: Buildings and places
brief: Generic buildings and landmarks types (not copies of real named landmarks).
notes: Building convention: front elevation standing on y (default 1600), params x,y,s,color,color2,anim(none/pop/lights),flip; ≤1000 px wide, ≤1450 px tall; no words (only 'H'/'P' where named), no red-cross emblem, generic not real landmarks. Skipped as covered: 'lighthouse building' (flat-vector/lighthouse), 'bus shelter' (flat-vector/bus-stop), 'radio tower' (flat-vector/antenna-tower), 'bridge arch' (flat-vector/bridge is an arched bridge). Slugs: tower->watchtower, park bench area->park-corner, monument obelisk->obelisk, colosseum-style arena->ancient-arena, billboard blank->billboard. Deleted in review, rebuild next run: hospital (garbled sign and ambulance bay), stadium (read as a top-down oval with a door), swimming pool (floating diving board, weak), playground (floating bars, sparse), oil rig (read as scaffolding), dam (read as a building next to water), temple (read as a tiered cake, no shikhara), diner (read as a train carriage). Fixed in review: nuclear-plant cooling towers given a real waist. Rebuilt 2026-11-18 (batch 11 run): hospital, stadium, swimming-pool, playground, oil-rig, dam, temple, diner.

title: Nature, plants, landscape and weather
brief: Plants, landscape elements, weather and sky objects.
notes: Nature convention: grounded scenery/props stand on y (1600 scenery, 1560 small props), anim none/pop/sway for plants, flow for water; sky and weather objects are type effect centred on x,y (default y 500); landscape pieces are ~1000 px wide vignettes on y, not full backgrounds. Skipped as covered: 'campfire' (flat-vector/fire-pit), 'egg' (nest has eggs; boiled-egg/fried-egg exist). 'log' is a single fallen log (logs = stack). Deleted in review, rebuild next run: rice paddy (read as a tiered cake), cliff (read as a grey striped building), waterfall (rock was a rounded grey box, read as a water tank). Fixed in review: dead-tree, jungle and playground scaled so nothing touches the frame edge; jungle lianas no longer hang below the ground; playground anim renamed lights -> swing. Run 2026-11-18 (with batch 12): cliff and waterfall rebuilt and kept; rice paddy deleted again (terraces read as a striped rug) – needs a clearer design, e.g. a hillside with stepped curved terraces and planted rows seen at an angle. Run 2026-11-18 (with batch 13): rice paddy rebuilt as a hillside with five curved stepped terraces, water, rice tufts and palms – kept.

title: Backgrounds and settings
brief: Full-frame parametric backgrounds (time of day, weather params) for common settings.
notes: Foundation: flat-vector/backdrop (type background, layer bg) – outdoor sky/land or indoor room generator with time (day/morning/dusk/night) and weather (clear/cloudy/rain/snow/fog/storm); exports Sky, Hills, Mountains, Skyline, TreeLine, Ground, WeatherFx, Window, Room, Lamp, Cloud, Stars, lit, mix, rnd. Every background preset imports it and has time/weather/anim params (weather shows through Window for interiors); centre stage x 220-860, y 1300-1750 kept clear. Note: the check preview draws the style's ground strip over the bottom of backgrounds; in stories use ground:false on shots with a full-frame background. Slugs renamed where a building/scenery part already existed: mall-interior, gym-interior, indoor-pool (swimming pool), police-station-interior, fire-station-interior, cave-interior; playground scene = playground-scene. Deleted in review, rebuild next run: airplane cabin (seat rows tiny at the edges, aisle dominated), car interior (road strip drawn inside the cabin), throne room (throne read as a yellow trophy/cake), podcast studio (too dark, mics too small to read). Fixed in review: moon-surface planet continents were floating in the sky; bus-interior/car-interior passed height instead of h to WeatherFx (rain covered the whole frame). Run 2026-11-18 (with batch 13): airplane-cabin, car-interior, throne-room and podcast-studio rebuilt and kept (airplane-cabin WeatherFx props fixed to numbers for tsc).

title: Sport, games, music and art
brief: Equipment and instruments.
notes: Prop convention as 06/07: handheld items hero size at s = 1 (~300-600 px), floor/room items 1 m ≈ 560 px; wall items centre on x,y; kite is a sky item on x,y; music-note is type effect on x,y. Skipped as covered: 'guitar' (= acoustic-guitar), 'camera art' (camera, dslr-camera, film-camera exist), 'vinyl' (vinyl-record), 'headphones music' (headphones). Trademark-free slugs: rubik cube -> puzzle-cube, frisbee -> flying-disc. clay pot wheel slug kept as clay-pot-wheel (name 'Pottery wheel'). Redrawn in review: electric-guitar and bass-guitar (body horns were floating wings), sitar (read as a banjo), clay-pot-wheel (read as a coffee grinder), whistle (body detached from lanyard), yo-yo (tiny disc with a spike), yoga-mat (thin line). Examples switched off intro anims so frame 0 is not empty: podium, chess-king, jigsaw-piece, soccer-goal, music-note. Deleted in review, rebuild next run: tuba (read as a coiled target, then as a bin with ring handles – draw an upright tuba with a big upturned bell, valve cluster and looped tubing), paint tubes (read as markers/sticks twice – draw large crimped-end tubes with caps, one squeezed). Note: bass-guitar is close to electric-guitar in silhouette (4 strings, longer neck). Run 2026-11-18 (with 14): tuba and paint-tubes drawn by the orchestrator and passed review.

title: Science, health, school and office
brief: Objects for explainers.
notes: Prop convention as 06/07: handheld items hero size at s = 1, floor items 1 m ≈ 560 px, wall items (x-ray, chalkboard, certificate, school-bell) centre on x,y; organs (heart-organ, brain, lungs, stomach, tooth, ear) are props centred on x,y; dna-helix, atom, molecule, compass-rose, eye, virus, bacteria, germ, blood-drop, heartbeat-line, percentage-sign are type effect on x,y. Skipped as covered (21): microscope science (microscope), magnet science (magnet), telescope science (telescope), wheelchair medical (wheelchair), soap bar (soap), first aid box (first-aid-kit), pencil/ruler/calculator/backpack/lunchbox school (pencil, ruler, calculator, backpack, lunchbox), calendar office (calendar), laptop office (laptop), trophy office (trophy), stopwatch office (stopwatch), rocket startup (rocket), lightbulb idea (light-bulb, anim on), gears idea (gear, gear-pair), puzzle idea (jigsaw-piece), coffee office (coffee-cup), target (arrow-target). Slugs: globe -> desk-globe (earth-globe is the planet effect), eraser board -> board-eraser, school bell -> wall gong (bell is the hand bell). Fixed in review: stomach, stethoscope (read as a slingshot) and crutch (single pole) redrawn by the orchestrator; desk-globe ring (looked like Saturn) replaced by a meridian arc; id-badge lanyard made a V strap; hospital-bed scaled to fit the frame. Trademark tags dropped: band-aid, post-it.

title: Faces, reactions and stickers
brief: Emoji-like expressive faces (original designs, not platform emoji), reaction stickers, hand gestures.
notes: Foundation (written by the orchestrator): flat-vector/reaction-face (type effect; round flat face with white die-cut sticker edge; eyes x16, mouth x20, brows, tears, extra effects, accessories, anim; exports ReactionFace) and flat-vector/text-sticker (word on a die-cut burst/star/circle/pill/cloud/speech/badge/tag shape, auto-fit text; exports TextSticker, shapePath). 48 face presets + 10 word presets (boom, pow, zap, 100/lol/wow/omg/new/sale/follow-sticker) import them. Batch look: every effect here is a die-cut sticker (white edge, soft shadow, one shade, pop-in from p.f, anim enum), centred on x,y (default 540,960). Hands take a skin param (default #FFC83D, or a SKIN name). thumbs-down reuses thumbs-up turned over. Deleted in review, rebuild next run: fist bump (fists tiny, burst dominated), praying hands (read as two bread rolls), handshake (hands merged into one blob) – draw them bigger, as two clearly separate hands with visible fingers and different sleeve colours. Fixed in review: anger-mark redrawn as four curved strokes (was a flower-like blob); pointing-hand and muscle-arm scaled up; shh-face finger redesigned so it cannot read as a rude gesture; tags frozen/goofy replaced. Run 16: fist-bump and praying-hands rebuilt; handshake still missing (see 16 notes).

title: Infographics, UI and motion text
brief: Style-free parts in parts/core/: charts with animated values, arrows, callouts, lower thirds, badges, counters, timelines, progress, maps pins. Use the style palette via p.style.
notes: Foundation (written by the orchestrator): core/stat-card is both a part and the shared kit for every core infographic (ui(style) palette from p.style: ink/accent/font + card, muted, soft, good, bad, warn, series[8]; startFrame(p) from `at`; enter/popIn/count/fmt/fitSize; Card, Txt; pathLen/drawDash/DrawPath for draw-on strokes). IMPORTANT: never use pathLength – resvg (previews, gallery, server SVG) ignores it; use DrawPath or drawDash(len, k). Built 103 core parts (charts, counters, lists, diagrams, maps, arrows, marks, frames, social UI, broadcast cards, badges, game HUD, particles and overlays). Fixed in review: 11 parts used pathLength (dotted/pale lines in previews) -> DrawPath/drawDash; loading-spinner arc; ticker-tape text sat on the band edge; box-frame interior was grey; unique clipPath ids for ticker/breaking-news. Deleted in review, rebuild next run: pointer hand (upright single finger with no thumb could read as a rude gesture – draw a clear index finger + visible thumb + curled fingers, default dir right), swipe gesture (hand unreadable), thumbs rating (blocky thumbs, down one unreadable – reuse simple icon shapes with a clear thumb), brush stroke (fringe tail looked like a comb). Also from 15: flat-vector/handshake deleted again (one paddle hand poking the other) – rebuild in flat-vector with clasped hands seen from the side, the top hand's fingers wrapping down over the back of the other. Run 17 (2026-11-19): flat-vector/handshake rebuilt (clasped from the side) and kept. pointer hand, swipe gesture, thumbs rating, brush stroke redrawn by a sub-agent and deleted again in review: pointer hand read as a 'finger gun' (thumb straight up) and dir up showed three raised fingers; swipe reused it; thumbs icons were blobs (down one read like a '9'); brush stroke tail was still a row of even spikes. Suggest the orchestrator draws these four itself next time. Run 18 (2026-11-19): the orchestrator drew the four itself and kept them: core/pointer-hand (outlined UI hand: straight index finger, three curled knuckles, thumb tucked along the side; dir right/left/up/down, point/tap; exports <Hand>), core/swipe-gesture (reuses <Hand>, finger-up hand slides with a trail and dashed arrow), core/thumbs-rating (two round buttons with a clear fist-and-thumb icon, the down one is the up icon mirrored vertically; pick fills and ticks the count; exports <Thumb>), core/brush-stroke (wavy swash with a loaded rounded start, uneven tapering dry-brush slivers, paints on with a growing clip). Batch 16 is done.

title: Fantasy, myth and sci-fi (original designs)
brief: Original creatures and sci-fi elements; nothing from existing franchises.
notes: Built 90 original fantasy/sci-fi parts (humanoids on the person generator, beasts on quadruped/bird looks, magic props, sci-fi tech, vehicles, space effects, spirits). Skipped as covered: flying saucer (=ufo), ringed planet (=planet), gold coins pile (=coins), vampire bat (=bat + vampire), fairy creature (flat-vector/fairy exists; a sub-agent overwrote it and it was restored). Renamed for IP safety: lightsaber-style beam sword -> beam-sword (crossguard hilt), kaiju-style monster -> giant-monster (not kept), space marine -> space-soldier, loch monster -> lake-monster. Deleted in review, rebuild next run: centaur (horse kept its own head with the torso mid-back - torso must replace the head/neck), skeleton warrior (white blob, no readable bones), ogre (shapeless body), giant-monster (jaw floated off the head), dragon egg (read as a cactus), escape pod (orange bean with a visor on legs read like a famous game crewmate - make it a cone/capsule with fins), jet bike (sled on stilts), wind spirit (looked like a stacked cake). Fixed in review: aliens no longer blink at f0; tree-spirit TS type error. Run 18 (2026-11-19): all 8 rebuilt by a sub-agent and kept after review: centaur (human torso rises from the chest end, no horse head/neck), skeleton-warrior (separate bones, helmet, shield, short sword), ogre, giant-monster (jaw part of the head), dragon-egg (smooth scaled oval in a nest), escape-pod (white cone capsule with fins and flame), jet-bike (wheel-less hover bike with twin jets), wind-spirit (spiral swirls with a face). Batch 17 is done.

title: Festivals, celebrations and clothing
brief: Celebrations from many cultures (generic, respectful) and clothing items.
notes: Built 85 flat-vector parts: festival props (diya, rangoli, firecracker, sparkler, fireworks, sky lanterns, paper lantern, Christmas, Hanukkah, Eid/Ramadan, Easter, Holi, party, wedding, New Year, harvest), cultural garments (turban and hijab on faceless display forms; saree, kurta, sherwani, kimono, hanbok on hangers) and clothing/accessories. Convention: garments are front-view catalogue items on a coat or clip hanger, hem on y, anim sway. Skipped as covered: christmas tree decorated (=christmas-tree), christmas gift (=gift-box), halloween pumpkin (=jack-o-lantern), cake candles (=birthday-cake), confetti (=core/confetti-burst), sunglasses item (=sunglasses), watch item (=watch), backpack item (=backpack), handbag item (=handbag), mask party (=carnival-mask). Renamed: kimono item -> kimono, hanbok item -> hanbok, umbrella item -> umbrella, pinata-style donkey -> pinata-donkey. Failed/deleted, rebuild next run: sandals (sub-agent: straps read as sticks/worms), mooncake (cut wedge read as a separate blob - draw a whole round fluted cake with an embossed flower, no wedge), high heels (red wedge on black stilts, unreadable - draw one clear stiletto pump in side view: pointed toe, arched sole, thin tall heel), helmet bike (blue blob - show vents as clear slots, a visor peak and chin straps), chinese dragon dance head (read as a worm/snake - draw a big boxy festival lion-dance-style head with a wide mouth, large eyes with lids, a single horn, fur trim, and a short draped cloth body). Fixed in review: tie redrawn (stripes now clipped to a proper tapered blade with a knot), tiara scaled up and made gold, red-envelope example no longer invisible at f0, belt TS readonly tuple error; trademark tags dropped: levis, stetson. Run 19 (2026-11-19): mooncake (whole fluted cake with embossed flower, on a plate), bike-helmet (vents, visor peak, chin straps) and dragon-dance-head (boxy red-gold head, single horn, fur trim, short scaled cloth body) rebuilt and kept. Deleted again: sandals (straps still read as teal worms) and high heels (red wedge on a stick). Both failed twice with Haiku - next run the orchestrator should draw them itself, or drop them. Run 20 (2026-11-19): sandals (top-view pair, cork soles, two wide buckled straps, heel strap) and high heels (single red stiletto pump, side view) drawn by the orchestrator and kept. Batch done.

title: Pixel art: style + people
brief: Create parts/pixel-art/style (16-colour palette, crisp square pixels drawn as SVG rects on a 4–8 px grid, shapeRendering crispEdges) and a parts/pixel-art/sprite generator (pixel map strings + palette, 2–4 frame animation), then people presets as small game-style sprites scaled up.
notes: New style pixel-art: parts/pixel-art/style (16-colour palette PAL, role chars s/h/t/i/l/z/a/j/q filled per part, Pixels renderer merging runs into crispEdges rects, auto one-cell outline, gridOf/stamp/fill/outlined helpers, blocky sky/ground decor, pixel title plate), pixel-art/sprite (generic pixel-map sprite generator, 1-4 frames, bob/bounce/float/shake/pulse) and pixel-art/person (layered front-facing game sprite, adult ~41 cells x 24 px: builds adult/teen/child/toddler, 14 hair styles, 28 hats, 14 tops, overlays, neckwear, 45 held items incl. chest items and ground poles, back gear, belly, chair/wheelchair seat, idle/walk/run/wave/cheer/jump/talk, free pixel `extra` overlays). Foundation drawn and reviewed by the orchestrator. All 120 people names built as person presets (LOOK spread under p, so every param can still override); doctor written by the orchestrator, the rest by 6 Haiku sub-agents via a preset helper. Fixed in review: librarian floating book stack removed, surveyor tripod moved to the ground, welder given a real welding mask, delivery rider given a cube bag on the back, musician given a trumpet (was an unreadable disc), firefighter recoloured to tan turnout coat + hi-vis bands, superhero kid recoloured to green suit + purple cape (avoid famous red/blue scheme). Next pixel-art batches can reuse pixel-art/sprite for animals, items and tiles.

title: Pixel art: animals
brief: Presets using parts/pixel-art/sprite.
notes: Built 103 pixel-art/sprite presets (side view facing right, role chars a/A/z with coat/coat2 params, pal override). Convention: legged animals stand on y with walk/run leg cels; birds add a fly anim (wing cels); fish anchor on the centre (centre=true, y 960) with a swim anim and example s 1. Template: pixel-art/dog drawn by the orchestrator. Rejected in review and redrawn the same run (kept): camel, llama, lamb, cheetah, leopard, jaguar, snow leopard, panda, yak, platypus, wombat, woodpecker (on a trunk segment), ostrich, emu, turkey, catfish, hammerhead shark, swordfish, pufferfish; shark stray belly cells fixed; all fish examples rescaled to s 1 (were cut off). Deleted after two tries, rebuild next run: kitten (came out as a huge upright orange figure - draw a small 4-legged kitten ~12 cells wide, big head), chipmunk (boxy - small squirrel shape with side stripes), toucan (black blob - needs a clearly separate head, white bib and a beak as long as the body), hummingbird (red throat drawn as a cross - draw the gorget as a small red patch under the beak), bluejay and cardinal (shapeless blobs - separate round head with crest, oval body, tail), magpie (black blob, tail never rendered). Small birds are the weak spot for Haiku: give them a written pixel map sketch or draw them yourself.

title: Pixel art: items and food
brief: Game-inventory style item sprites using parts/pixel-art/sprite.

title: Pixel art: tiles and backgrounds
brief: Tiled backgrounds and scenery (grass, water, brick, sky with clouds, dungeon, city, forest, space) built from tiles.

title: Ink sketch: style + people
brief: Create parts/ink-sketch/style (hand-drawn black ink line on off-white paper, slight wobble from the engine boil, one accent colour wash) and a parts/ink-sketch/person generator (line-art figure with poses and expressions), then presets.

title: Ink sketch: animals
brief: Line-art animals with a light colour wash.

title: Ink sketch: objects
brief: Line-art objects, vehicles and nature elements.

title: Ink sketch: settings, faces and gestures
brief: Simple sketched settings plus expressive faces and hand gestures for explainers.

title: Storybook: more history people and props
brief: Extend the existing storybook style (reuse storybook/figure where possible; add new figures if needed) with history archetypes and period props.

title: Core: motion text, transitions and effects
brief: Style-free animated text treatments and screen effects (all SVG): kinetic typography, wipes, reveals, overlays.
